title: Aurora Effects: Scene Definition File (wave 1)
description: Wire shape for one scene definition file, games/sonic4/data/editor/effects/<scene_id>.json (aeon repo, editor-owned tree). NORMATIVE for shape only: which keys exist, their JSON types and ranges; docs/AURORA_EFFECTS_SCHEMA.md is normative for semantics, and semantic validation of authored VALUES belongs to sigil: tools/effects_gen.py (aeon) emits generated .emp calling the scene DSL constructors, so every ensure and scene_budget_enforce fires on authored content at build time. CLOSED on the writer path (unevaluatedProperties: false, the bus request-path precedent): on this path the party validating is the party publishing what it writes; wave-2 keys (presets, effectsRef, variants, cycles, fires, reserved in the doc's section 7) enter by amending this schema, never by unilateral emission. Aurora's writer-side golden validates against this file and is pinned against BOTH repo SHAs (empyrean + aeon) per the doc's section 8.

factor.description: A packed shift-add scroll factor (engine/level/parallax_dsl.emp). Either a published FACTOR_* const name emitted verbatim into the constructor call, or a custom packed() triple: s1=15 means term zero (locked), s2=15 means single-term, op 0=add / 1=subtract the second term.

tableRef.description: A 256-byte signed deform/column table: a DSL generator call, or a raw .bin (path relative to games/sonic4/data/editor/effects/, no .. segments; baked via embed(), the inject_editor_bg precedent). No registry-symbol form in wave 1 (deliberate; see doc section 2.4).

layerDeform.description: Per-layer H-deform attachment (SceneDeform at layer level): "none" or Own(table, shift_a, shift_b, phase, speed). When own is present the layer's dsa/dsb/phase must be absent or at defaults, since they lower into the same record fields (two-sources guard; sigil enforces).

sceneDeform.description: Scene-level shared H-deform attachment (SceneDeform.Shared): "none" or one table both planes sample.

drift.description: Time-driven drift of this layer: a constant horizontal rate added to the band's scroll every frame, independent of the camera (S1 GHZ clouds, S2 WFZ/HTZ clouds, S3K AIZ1 clouds). "none" or absent = the layer does not drift (lowers to a zero tail). rate is a signed integer in units of 1/256 px per FRAME: 1 px/frame = 256; S3K AIZ1's clouds = 32; corpus max 6 px/frame = 1536. The bound +/-4096 (16 px/frame) is a taste bound, not a correctness bound. 0 is refused (indistinguishable from none in ROM; aeon refuses Rate(0) at build time, scene_dsl.emp layer() ensure). UNIT HAZARD: an author writing 1 meaning 1 px/frame gets 1/256 px/frame; the editor SHOULD present px/frame and multiply by 256 on export. Engine contract: aeon docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-29-band-drift-design.md section 7 rows 1, 2 and 10 at aeon e0ce6011; the field is authorable only once aeon's CAP_BAND_DRIFT emission parcel lands (the bit arrives WITH its gated block), and until then effects_gen.py refuses the key.

rowRemap.description: EFFECTS-W1 item 9's ROW REMAP (added 2026-09-04, docs/AURORA_EFFECTS_SCHEMA.md section 2.6, aeon key-shape artifact 3d917657 docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-04-item9-row-remap-key-shape.md, against the landed constructor SceneRemap.Ladder(t, y, h) at aeon d8baf84f engine/level/scene_dsl.emp:518-521). This layer's plane-B scroll words are re-fetched through a perspective-selected index ladder, so screen line i of the band takes the value that belonged to line ladder[i]; the band compresses toward the surface as the camera separates the background's picture of the surface from the foreground's truth about it. "none" or absent = this layer's plane-B scroll words are whatever the line loops wrote (every shipped layer but one); absent and "none" lower to the same eight bytes (a NULL ladder), so the distinction is an authoring one: "none" says the author chose no remap. Lowers to layer(rowRemap: SceneRemap.Ladder(<ladder derived from height_shift>, plane_y, height_shift)); both numbers forwarded VERBATIM, 1:1, no conversion on either side. THE LADDER IS NOT NAMED HERE: it is derived from height_shift (one number, one source; aeon scene_dsl.emp:879's two-sources rule). ladder and table are RESERVED and refused by name below; a named non-perspective ladder is a future second oneOf arm, not in this contract. It is the ONLY thing that raises CAP_ROW_REMAP, and the anchor channel comes from the SCENE's own anchor key, never from the layer (scene_dsl.emp:822-824). REFUSALS THIS SCHEMA DOES NOT ENCODE, owned by aeon's generator tools/effects_gen.py and re-stated as engine ensures for hand-authored scenes (scene_dsl.emp:1907, :1913, :1920): a remapped layer needs something to vary (its own curve, or a live dsb with a deform_bg table, or the scene anchor's live dsb with a deform_bg table), else the remap is the identity and the effect is ABSENT; the scene MUST declare anchor; at most ONE layer per scene may carry rowRemap; the game must raise CAP_ROW_REMAP. Verified in aeon SOURCE at d8baf84f that a document-bound section can seed the channel it needs (preset.emp:153-154, :283-290; effects_gen.py:1280-1281); no ROM has been built through this path yet, so the first 9c parcel builds it.

plane_y.description: The BG PLANE LINE at which this layer's ART paints the surface. NOT a world Y and NOT a screen line: the runtime computes the background's image of the surface as (plane_y - Vscroll_BG); it is a different number from the layer's own world_y. Same coordinate space as vsplit.at. THIS SCHEMA IS THE ONLY ENFORCEMENT OF THE 511 CEILING: aeon's ensure at scene_dsl.emp:1008 tests >= 0 only, brm_plane_y is u16 (parallax.emp:420), so 512..65535 would emit a silently-wrong window (aeon row ROWREMAP-PLANEY-CEILING).

height_shift.description: A SHIFT, NOT A LINE COUNT: H = 1 << height_shift. 4 is a 16-line ladder (272 B), 6 is 64 lines (4,160 B, S3K LBZ2's own height), 7 is 128 lines (16,512 B); the ladder is (H+1) rows of H bytes, quadratic in H. Aeon refuses 0..2 and 8+ at build time (scene_dsl.emp:1006). UNIT HAZARD: an editor may DISPLAY 1 << height_shift beside the control and MUST EXPORT the shift; every value 3..7 is legal, so a conversion bug lands as a band four times too tall, not as a refusal. TODAY ONLY 4 BUILDS: row_remap_ladder16() (aeon parallax_dsl.emp:220) is the one ladder the engine can generate until 9b's generator lands; the generator refuses the other four by name meanwhile.

ladder.description: RESERVED, refused by name: the ladder is derived from height_shift; a named ladder is the second-variant extension and is not in this contract yet.

table.description: RESERVED, refused by name: see ladder.

v_factor.description: Whole-plane Plane-B vertical scroll, as a RIGHT-SHIFT AMOUNT, not a packed factor. The engine computes target_b = ((camY - v_center) >> v_factor) + v_offset (engine/level/parallax.emp). 15 is the LOCK SENTINEL: it is tested before the shift and pins the BG plane to v_offset regardless of the camera. This is a different space from a layer's fa/fb, where locked is the packed value $0FF; do not spell this field with a FACTOR_* name.

v_center.description: World Y the vertical mapping is centred on; same space as a layer's world_y. 0..32767: camera Y is clamped to 0..act extent and every act asserts extent <= 32768, so a value of $8000 or above would read negative after the sub.w (engine/level/parallax.emp, Parallax_Step5_Vscroll). Bounded 2026-08-26 with aeon's VOFFSET landing, on the v_factor precedent.

v_offset.description: SIGNED vertical scroll offset in pixels, added after the shift: target_b = ((camY - v_center) >> v_factor) + v_offset, a 16-bit add.w into Vscroll_BG (the locked plane pins Vscroll_BG to it). It was always signed in the engine math; the unsigned field type was the error. Bounded 2026-08-26 with aeon's VOFFSET landing.

v_factor_fg.description: Plane-A counterpart of v_factor, same shift encoding. RESERVED in the v1 runtime (the pipeline always sets fg_vscroll = camY, engine/structs.emp) and authored for identity only. Typed here so a v2 that starts consuming it does not inherit the packed-factor mistake.

bob_shift.description: The scene-level vertical bob's AMPLITUDE, as a right-shift of the 256-amplitude sine table: peak excursion 256 >> bob_shift px (1 = 128 px, 8 = 1 px). 15 is the NO-BOB SENTINEL and the default (the same 15 that means no deform on pcfg_anchor_dsa/dsb); 0 and 9..14 are refused by scene() (engine/level/scene_dsl.emp), so this schema admits exactly 15 or 1..8. HAZARD: the wire byte pcfg_bob is 0 for no bob and (bob_shift << 4) | bob_period otherwise, so document-off (15) and wire-off (0) are opposite ends of the range; never clamp toward 0 or write 0 for off. Added 2026-08-30 with aeon 8c75722b (DoD item 7); docs/AURORA_EFFECTS_SCHEMA.md section 2.5.

bob_period.description: The vertical bob's PERIOD, as a right-shift of the logic tick: sine index (Logic_Tick.low >> bob_period) & $FF, so one full sway is 256 << bob_period ticks (256 at 0, about 4.3 s at 60 Hz; 65,536 at 8). 8 is the ceiling: the 256-entry cycle still closes inside the 16-bit counter, one shift further and the background jumps by the full amplitude once per wrap. Ignored when bob_shift is 15. Added 2026-08-30 with aeon 8c75722b; docs/AURORA_EFFECTS_SCHEMA.md section 2.5.

reels.description: The REELS: up to five independently scrolling 64-pixel-wide vertical background strips, the slot-machine-reel demo (aeon games/sonic4/data/effects/ojz_effects.emp OJZ_Reels_Fill), authorable and bindable per scene for the first time. Added 2026-09-04 (docs/AURORA_EFFECTS_SCHEMA.md section 2.7, EFFECTS-W1 DoD item 10's authoring half, DEBUG TIER, against aeon's decision note docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-04-reels-per-scene-key-shape.md at aeon 660aabc0, which defers to the survey docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-03-item10a-reels-key-shape.md). DEBUG-ONLY, and no JSON keyword can say so: the mechanism's table, proc and on-switch all sit inside if DEBUG == 1 (OJZ_Reel_Speed's length is 0 in release, ojz_effects.emp:1766-1767; the only writer of OJZ_Reel_Active is tools/reels_witness.py), so a scene saved with reels shows NOTHING in a release build and the editor panel must say so on screen. Not capability-gated: no CAP_ bit exists for reels, and a generator arm must not emit a check that does not exist. ONE MEMBER, rates: EXACTLY FIVE signed integers, -128..127, pairwise distinct, in SCREEN ORDER: index i owns column-pairs 4i..4i+3, screen X 64i..64i+63 (the column-to-band map is a hardcoded lsr.b #2, ojz_effects.emp:1817); an editor that sorts or round-trips rates through a dict keyed by band name silently relocates every strip, so the generator emits in document order, verbatim. UNIT: SIGNED WHOLE PIXELS PER FRAME, no fixed point anywhere on the path (add.b (a2)+, d0 into a byte phase that wraps mod 256; a strip's phase cycles every 256/|rate| frames, so 3 is a 1.4 s reel, 16 is fast and legible, 64 and up is a strobe; the useful slider range is about -16..16 and that is UI guidance, never a refusal). PROHIBITION: drift.rate's x256 export conversion MUST NOT be applied here; a panel copied from the drift panel would emit 768 for an intended 3, and this -128..127 bound is the ONLY place that mistake is caught today (the engine has no magnitude ensure; aeon's implementing parcel adds one beside the generated table, section 2.7). ZERO IS ALLOWED, deliberately unlike drift.rate: a stationary strip among moving ones is a real authored choice; uniqueItems caps it at one. The geometry is FIXED at 5 strips of 4 column-pairs: REEL_BAND_COUNT and REEL_COLS_PER_BAND (games/sonic4/config/constants.emp:66-67) size a RAM array and are compiled into a shift, so a band count is a code shape, not a field; minItems/maxItems 5 is a COPY of that constant and aeon's generator re-derives it from constants.emp and refuses a disagreeing length. ABSENT = no reels for this scene (v_deform's absent-key precedent); there is no 'none' spelling, because the binding table is generated whole and 'keep' and 'off' are the same state for it. BINDING (section 2.7): the generator emits one DEBUG-gated [i8; REEL_BAND_COUNT] table per authoring scene plus an association table keyed on the scene's lowered config label, matched at runtime against Parallax_Current_Config; that label is unique ONLY for a section bound at Effects_ResolveParallax's rung 1 (an editor sceneRef, preset.emp:190-195), so the generator REFUSES a reels key on a scene whose sections resolve through a preset (rung 2) or the act default (rung 3), where the pointer is shared and the rates would silently reach other sections. What an author sees: each strip's BACKGROUND scrolls at its own rate, the foreground is untouched by construction (the FG word is copied unchanged, ojz_effects.emp:1813), and the excursion is 0..255 px below the camera's BG base, always downward; a negative rate reverses the travel, it does not lift the strip.

rates.description: Five signed whole-pixel-per-frame rates in screen order, left strip first. Pairwise distinct (two strips sharing a rate read as one wide strip; the engine's distinct5 ensure guards the hand table, and the generated table gets the same guard from aeon's implementing parcel). -128..127 is the i8 the table is declared as and, until aeon's ensure lands, the only enforcement of it. No x256.
